subject: Lexical elements
notes: Rule 5 (cite.py --check 8.3.5 "The opening delimiter shall be immediately preceded by a space, left parenthesis, or opening pseudo-text delimiter" OK 5)). kb/Work PB1394 LANDED (wave 73 group A): SeparatorRule asks every literal token of either lexer mode (LiteralTokens.Types, the set LiteralScreenDriftTests derives from the grammar) whether the character before its opening delimiter is a space, '(' or '==' and the character after its closing delimiter is a space, ',', ';', '.', ')' or '==', and reports COBOL2633 otherwise; touching literals are one report. The prefixed opening delimiters (X" N" B" NX" BX") are now always delimited as one token whatever their content (PB1441), so W"AB" beside an item W is IDENTIFIER + literal and reported, and X"GG" is a malformed hexadecimal literal (COBOL2630) rather than X + "GG". The parse-recovery guesses COBOL0301/COBOL0302 that stated the rule a second time are removed. Negative: DISPLAY "AB"N, MOVE"AB", IF "AB"=A -> COBOL2633 at all four editions.
